facts.text: Hattiesburg was founded in 1882 by Captain William H. Hardy and named after his wife Hattie.
The city grew at the junction of the Leaf and Bouie rivers, where the Gulf and Ship Island Railroad and the New Orleans and Northeastern Railroad met.
Hattiesburg is home to the University of Southern Mississippi, founded as Mississippi Normal College, and William Carey University, making it a prominent university town.
In 2011, the Hattiesburg Historic Neighborhood District earned a spot on the American Planning Association’s “Great Places In America” list.
The African American Military History Museum, located in Hattiesburg, preserves the legacy of black soldiers from the region.
Hattiesburg played a pivotal role in the 1960s civil rights movement, with leaders like Vernon Dahmer leading protests that helped overturn voting‑rights convictions.
